report.title: Dependency confusion and registry index poisoning against the resolver
report.question: If a public registry offers a package with the same name (or a higher version) as a private/internal one, which does the resolver choose - and can an index entry be added or altered without detection?
report.headline_answer: SPLIT BY LAYER, decided by artifact hash and machine gate code. (1) The resolver CHOOSES the shadow: registry.resolve is version-only and publisher-blind, so a public 'hello-skill@9.9.9' from an untrusted publisher is selected over the private 1.1.0 (resolved payload_digest == the ATTACKER digest). (2) An index entry CAN be added or altered without detection AT THE RESOLVER LAYER: registry.load_index validates only the JSON schema, so a tampered payload_digest or manifest_path loads and resolves to the injected value. BUT (3) the gated installer DEFEATS both attacks end-to-end: name-shadowing dies at gate 2 publisher-known (MKT-I02) so the attacker artifact is never fetched (nothing on disk), and index poisoning dies at gate 1 index-signature (MKT-I01) for any unsigned edit and at gate 3 manifest cross-check (MKT-I03) even for a maintainer-re-signed edit to payload_digest or permissions. Net: dependency confusion and index poisoning SUCCEED against the bare resolver surface (registry.resolve/search/load_index) and are REFUTED against the 13-gate install.Installer. The one in-repo ungated reader is the `mkt search` CLI (cli.py:233-234), which would DISPLAY a poisoned entry; the only consumer that FETCHES a payload is the gated Installer (install.py:527).

resolved_resolver_identity.source_precedence_rule: registry.resolve: candidates filtered by name (+optional channel/yanked) only, winner = versions.best = highest semver; publisher-BLIND (registry.py:195-207). Federation (FederatedView.resolve) tries primary then mirrors by priority; a verify-and-require-primary-index mirror must match the primary on (name,version,manifest_digest).
resolved_resolver_identity.index_integrity_control: the index is signed with a registry-maintainer ed25519 key; enforced ONLY at install gate 1 (verify_index_signature, registry.py:96-107 / install.py:280-286). load_index/resolve/search apply NO signature check. Package manifests are independently signed; gate 3 cross-checks the index row's payload_digest and permissions against the SIGNED manifest (install.py:319-337).
resolved_resolver_identity.fixture: fixture.build() -> reg:fixture-local, a filesystem registry with real RFC-8032 ed25519 signatures over canonical bytes; hello-skill@1.0.0(stable) + @1.1.0(beta) from the trusted pub:alpha-tools are the private package.

verdicts_by_target.target: T1 -- resolver chooses a same-name higher-version public/shadow entry over the private one
T2 -- the name-shadowing attack reaches disk (attacker artifact fetched/installed) end-to-end
T3 -- an index entry can be added/altered and accepted by the resolver (load_index/resolve) without detection
T4 -- index poisoning reaches disk (installer accepts a tampered/added entry) end-to-end
